sources.name: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.role: RDF/OWL provenance entity, activity, agent, derivation, association and qualified-relation contract
verified_facts: PROV-O expresses the PROV Data Model using OWL2 classes, properties and restrictions for representing and interchanging provenance.
PROV-O distinguishes Entity, Activity and Agent and supports relations such as generation, usage, derivation and activity association.
Qualified relations can carry details such as role and time beyond an unqualified provenance relation.
semantic_limits: An RDF provenance assertion is not evidence that the described activity actually ran or that the referenced source bytes were read.
An Agent or association statement allocates modeled responsibility; it does not authenticate the agent or certify measurement accuracy.
A provenance location may be a directory, row or other non-geographic place and must not be treated as exact HMLR geometry.

sources.name: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.role: entity generation, activity usage, derivation influence, attribution and event-time contract
verified_facts: An entity is a physical, digital, conceptual or other thing with fixed aspects and an identifier can refer to those fixed aspects.
Generation is completion of producing an entity and usage is the beginning of an activity utilizing an entity.
Derivation connects a generated entity to a used entity but usage and generation alone are not sufficient; influence is also required.
semantic_limits: A source and output appearing in one activity record must not automatically be asserted as a derivation without evidence of influence.
A generation statement does not prove immutable source identity, complete byte consumption or successful numeric measurement.
PROV-DM models provenance semantics; it does not define parcel containment, CRS, vertical datum, terrain units or accuracy tolerance.

sources.name: Constraints of the PROV Data Model
sources.role: valid provenance instance, uniqueness, typing, event ordering and consistency contract
verified_facts: Valid PROV instances satisfy definitions, inferences and constraints intended to represent a consistent history.
The constraints include uniqueness rules for generation and invalidation and typing or impossible-overlap checks.
Event ordering requires generation to precede usage and invalidation, and usage to precede invalidation.
semantic_limits: A valid PROV instance is internally consistent provenance, not proof that its statements correspond to real-world execution.
Ordering and uniqueness constraints do not prove source authority, digest equality, complete download or measurement accuracy.
Normalization or equivalence of provenance documents must not create a business row without external measurement evidence.

sources.name: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.role: data graph, shapes graph, validation report, result severity and conformance contract
verified_facts: SHACL validation takes a data graph and shapes graph and produces a validation report; conformance checking produces a boolean outcome.
A validation report records sh:conforms and validation results such as focus node, severity and source constraint component.
A processor may support limiting returned validation results and shapes-graph well-formedness checking is not strictly required.
semantic_limits: sh:conforms true only states that no result was produced for the supplied shapes and processor behavior; it does not prove source truth or measurement accuracy.
A limited validation report is not a complete audit of every potential defect or every unmodeled requirement.
SHACL syntax and constraint conformance do not establish exact parcel geometry, source bytes, CRS, vertical datum or height semantics.
